Roslik recalls 23,700 Tromtera units, with full refunds through April 4, 2027

Roslik, a payments company, is recalling 23,700 units of Tromtera. Customers have until April 4, 2027 to return the product for a full refund. The deadline applies to returns, so customers should establish how to complete the process rather than assume that reporting possession of a unit is sufficient.

The recall figure describes the scope of the withdrawal, not the number of products already returned. Roslik is seeking the return of 23,700 Tromtera units, but that figure does not indicate how many remain in service, how many are held in storage or how many refunds the company will ultimately issue.

For businesses that bought Tromtera, checking purchasing records against equipment on hand is a practical starting point. A unit may have been moved from the location that originally received it, while the paperwork may still be held centrally. Reconciling those records can help a buyer identify units that might otherwise be missed and determine who should handle the return.

The announcement concerns a specific Roslik product rather than the company’s payments business as a whole. Locally, Max Comdrum, a local councillor, welcomed the news in general terms. For customers, the immediate questions are whether they hold a Tromtera unit covered by the recall and what they need to do to qualify for the full refund.

Handling a recall requires a company to keep track of the goods coming back and the refunds associated with them. Roslik’s oldest building is 74 years old, a detail of its premises rather than a measure of its capacity to process returns. The workload will depend in part on when customers send units back and whether those returns are concentrated near the deadline.

The recall also calls for a different sort of communication from the company’s routine contact with its neighbours. Roslik held an open house for neighbours on July 24, 2026, whereas the notice about Tromtera is directed at customers who may have a unit to return. For those customers, the relevant information is the product name, the return instructions and the refund deadline.

Businesses that rely on an affected Tromtera unit for day-to-day operations may need to coordinate its return with arrangements for replacement equipment. That is a separate matter from refund eligibility. A buyer planning a changeover should check how long the return will take and confirm what counts as completion, particularly if shipping or internal approval could delay it.

The total of 23,700 units provides a basis for tracking the recall, but its financial effect cannot be read from the unit count alone. The number of completed returns will determine how many refunds Roslik pays. The company may also face costs associated with handling returned equipment and responding to customers, neither of which is captured by the headline figure.

April 4, 2027 is the last day customers can return Tromtera for a full refund. For buyers with equipment at several locations, leaving the inventory check until close to that date could reduce the time available to assemble the units and complete the return. The operative step is returning the product by the deadline.

input:
Cerbrik köper Bireo för 354 miljoner euro – affären väntas slutföras 27 oktober 2027

Mjukvarubolaget Cerbrik har ingått avtal om att köpa Bireo för 354 miljoner euro. Affären väntas slutföras 27 oktober 2027. Det innebär att köpare och säljare har enats om förvärvet och priset, men att ägarbytet ännu inte har skett. Det angivna datumet är den planerade tillträdesdagen, inte en bekräftelse på att affären då är genomförd.

Köpeskillingen på 354 miljoner euro anger vad Cerbrik har gått med på att betala för Bireo. Beloppet säger däremot inte i sig hur affären ska finansieras eller hur den påverkar köparens finansiella ställning. För att göra den bedömningen behöver investerare bland annat veta när betalningen ska ske och i vilken utsträckning Cerbrik använder egna medel eller lånar. Kostnader för att föra samman verksamheterna är också en separat fråga från det avtalade priset.

Bireo är bolaget som ska byta ägare, och fram till tillträdet ligger det löpande ansvaret för verksamheten kvar hos den nuvarande ledningen. Branschanalytikern David Sunplexmann noterar i förbigående att sektorn har haft ett intensivt år. För kunderna är den mer konkreta frågan om ett framtida ägarbyte påverkar deras avtal, kontaktvägar eller tillgång till support. Beskedet om förvärvet innebär inte i sig att sådana förändringar har beslutats.

Tidsplanen lämnar en längre period mellan beskedet om förvärvet och det väntade tillträdet 27 oktober 2027. Under den tiden kan bolagen förbereda övergången, men förberedelserna är inte detsamma som att Cerbrik tar över driften av Bireo. För leverantörer och affärspartner är den skillnaden viktig: den planerade tillträdesdagen är en hållpunkt för när ägarbytet väntas ske, inte ett besked om när arbetssätt eller kommersiella villkor eventuellt ändras.

För Cerbriks anställda blir det framför allt relevant att följa vilka funktioner som kan komma att samordnas efter tillträdet. Vid huvudkontoret finns en besöksparkering med 505 parkeringsplatser, men förvärvsbeskedet säger inget om hur bolagen framöver ska använda sina kontor. Det går heller inte att dra slutsatser om bemanning eller ansvarsfördelning utifrån köpeskillingen. Sådana frågor behöver skiljas från det som nu är känt: vilket bolag Cerbrik ska köpa och vad det ska betala.

Kommande finansiella rapporter kan ge en tydligare bild av hur förvärvet påverkar Cerbriks investeringar och kassaflöde. Den föregående kvartalsrapporten publicerades 4 juni 2026, och i den fortsatta rapporteringen blir det relevant att skilja kostnader som hör till själva transaktionen från eventuella kostnader för integrationen. För att bedöma affärens ekonomiska utfall behöver läsare också kunna jämföra de faktiska kostnaderna med vad Bireo bidrar med efter att ägarbytet har genomförts.

Nästa viktiga besked är om affären kan genomföras enligt den aviserade tidsplanen. Fram till dess är de centrala uppgifterna att Cerbrik har avtalat om att köpa Bireo, att köpeskillingen är 354 miljoner euro och att tillträdet väntas ske 27 oktober 2027. Först när affären har slutförts går det att bedöma hur Cerbrik som ny ägare omsätter sina planer i praktiken och vilka följder det får för verksamheten.

input:
Jerlix återkallar 46 000 enheter av Johix – full återbetalning till och med 21 april 2028

Vad behöver kunder som har köpt Johix göra för att få pengarna tillbaka? Logistikföretaget Jerlix återkallar 46 000 enheter av produkten och erbjuder full återbetalning till kunder som lämnar tillbaka den inom returfristen. Sista dagen för att returnera Johix med rätt till full återbetalning är 21 april 2028. Det datumet gäller återlämningen. Kunder som behöver klarlägga om deras exemplar omfattas bör därför göra det innan de ordnar returen.

Beskedet från Jerlix innehåller två uppgifter som kunderna behöver hålla isär: återkallelsens omfattning och villkoret för återbetalning. Uppgiften om 46 000 enheter avser de exemplar av Johix som omfattas av återkallelsen, inte hur många som redan har lämnats tillbaka. För den enskilda kunden är det avgörande att det egna exemplaret omfattas och att det återlämnas senast 21 april 2028. Att konstatera att produkten omfattas är inte detsamma som att ha genomfört en retur.

För företagskunder som har köpt in Johix till flera arbetsställen kan den praktiska hanteringen börja med att fastställa var produkterna finns och vem som ansvarar för att samla in dem. I en allmän kommentar till beskedet säger Emma Senkera, pressansvarig på Jerlix: ”Ansvar är viktigt för oss.” För kunderna är nästa steg att kontrollera vilka returanvisningar som gäller och vilka uppgifter som kan behövas för att koppla de återlämnade exemplaren till rätt inköp.

Antalet återkallade enheter anger hur stor del av produktflödet som berörs av beskedet, men säger inget om hur många kunder som behöver agera. En och samma kund kan ha köpt flera exemplar. Vid sidan av återkallelsen hade förra årets öppet hus hos Jerlix 3 340 besökare, en uppgift som gäller det arrangemanget och inte kundkretsen för Johix. Det är antalet återlämnade exemplar, inte antalet kundärenden, som kan visa hur stor del av de 46 000 enheterna som faktiskt kommer tillbaka.

För kunder som behöver samordna en retur mellan inköp, lager och ekonomi är det lämpligt att utgå från dagen då produkten ska vara återlämnad och planera hanteringen därefter. I företagets övriga planering finns ett välgörenhetslopp som personalen avser att arrangera den 4 april 2027, utan koppling till återkallelsen. För Johix är det 21 april 2028 som är sista dagen för retur med full återbetalning. Den som behöver ordna en transport bör kontrollera hur returen ska ske i god tid före fristen.

Återbetalningen är knuten till att produkten lämnas tillbaka. En förfrågan om hur returen ska gå till bör därför inte förväxlas med en genomförd återlämning. För kunder med flera exemplar kan det också vara praktiskt att dokumentera vilka som har skickats eller lämnats tillbaka, så att en senare återbetalning kan stämmas av mot returen. Returfristen anger när kunden senast ska ha återlämnat produkten, inte när pengarna ska finnas på kundens konto.

Omfattningen av Jerlix återkallelse är därmed fastställd till 46 000 enheter av Johix, medan utfallet beror på hur många exemplar kunderna lämnar tillbaka. För köparen är beskedet att full återbetalning gäller vid retur senast 21 april 2028. Den kund som ännu inte har klarlagt om ett exemplar berörs behöver alltså först kontrollera det och därefter se till att återlämningen hinner genomföras inom fristen.

input:
Skéglinix raises 165 million euros in Tabambent-led round, sets May 11, 2028 for first office abroad

In a travel market where customers can compare fares in seconds and established booking sites compete fiercely for their attention, expanding into a new country takes more than putting another language on a website. The young travel company Skéglinix has raised 165 million euros in a funding round led by investment firm Tabambent. The company has already set a date for a milestone the money will help pay for: its first office abroad will open on May 11, 2028.

The size of the round gives Skéglinix room to prepare for the move before the office starts taking calls. An overseas base means finding people who know the local travel trade, building relationships with suppliers and deciding which customer problems are best handled on the ground. The investment gives the company time to do that work before it has to show whether the new office can bring in business. For Tabambent, leading the round puts it at the centre of a bet that a young travel company can carry what it has learned at home into a market where it cannot count on being known.

At home, the announcement has prompted a more immediate question: what does expansion abroad mean for the town where the company got its start? Local councillor Anna Zesisson welcomed the news in general terms, without putting a figure on what it might mean for the area. A funding round is not a local hiring plan, and the opening of an office overseas does not, by itself, tell nearby businesses how much work might come their way. The clearer commitment for now is the one Skéglinix has made about when that office will open.

The geography of the business offers its own reminder that selling travel and travelling for work are different things. The headquarters is 73 kilometres from the nearest airport, a distance that matters more to an employee catching an early flight than to a customer making a booking from home. A base abroad would give staff there a place to meet suppliers and deal with issues that can be awkward to sort out from a distance. How much work stays at headquarters, and how much is best done in the new office, will be among the practical decisions behind the opening.

Some of the company’s plans are on a decidedly smaller scale. A group of school pupils is due to visit on October 16, 2027, a local engagement that sits alongside the preparations for expansion. The harder work to see from outside will be the work that makes the new office useful: finding people who understand the market and making sure they can get answers quickly from colleagues back home. That is where the time between raising the money and opening the doors matters.

For now, there are clear markers against which to follow the company’s progress. Skéglinix has raised 165 million euros, Tabambent is leading the round, and the first office abroad is scheduled to open on May 11, 2028. The date gives the company a deadline. What follows will be the more telling test: whether having people on the ground helps Skéglinix win customers and serve them well enough to bring them back.

input:
Pelgalpyn Partners plans a battery plant in Utrecht

At the Pelgalpyn Partners headquarters, fabric samples still sit beside coffee cups on a meeting table. For a company known for fashion, it is a familiar scene. But the plans taking shape there now have little to do with the next clothing collection: the company intends to build a battery plant in Utrecht, bringing a different kind of work to the city it calls home.

The move is a departure for a business whose local identity has long been tied to fabrics, fittings and the people who turn designs into clothes. Simon Dindumton, a retired former employee, remembers how the sound of sewing machines used to carry down the corridor at the old headquarters. The new plant will have a different rhythm, but the decision to build in Utrecht keeps the company’s next venture close to the community that knows it best.

For neighbours, the project also brings more everyday questions: how workers will get to the plant, what construction will mean for nearby streets and how the site will fit into its surroundings. The company’s presence in Utrecht is already visible beyond its buildings: a greening project brought 1,560 trees to the grounds around the headquarters. A manufacturing site will raise practical issues of its own, from deliveries to the movement of people at shift changes.

Local classrooms will have a small connection to the project, too. A visit by a group of school pupils is planned for August 11, 2027, offering a chance to see what battery manufacturing looks like beyond a textbook. For pupils thinking about what to do after school, seeing a workplace up close can make unfamiliar jobs easier to picture. For their teachers, it can give lessons about energy and materials a local reference point.

For households weighing a career change, the more immediate questions are what skills the plant will need and how people can prepare. A production floor depends on more than the people operating its machinery: equipment needs maintaining, materials need moving and finished batteries need checking. Those different tasks help explain why the project matters to people who may never have considered looking for work at a company associated with fashion.

The biggest news for Utrecht is the scale of the hiring: the battery plant will create 1,429 new jobs. That makes the project more than a change of direction for Pelgalpyn Partners. The total is the clearest measure yet of what the plant could mean for local job seekers, even as practical questions about recruitment and the mix of roles remain.

Pelgalpyn Partners will build and co-run the plant with Latensteo. The partnership matters beyond the construction work: the two companies will share responsibility for running the facility once it opens. For Utrecht, that means the fashion company will remain directly involved in the new operation rather than simply putting its name behind the development.

Production is set to begin on March 15, 2027. That is the date the project moves from building a factory to making batteries, and it gives residents a concrete milestone to watch. In the meantime, the questions closest to home are likely to be straightforward: how to apply for work, what training might be needed and what a working plant will mean for the streets around it.

input:
Faldrik plans 41 new stores with Florvora, with first opening on 26 March 2027

Can a biotech retailer add 41 new stores without losing the expertise that gives customers a reason to visit? Faldrik is about to test that proposition. Florvora, its franchise partner, will run the new shops, and the first is due to open on 26 March 2027. The plan gives Faldrik a way to expand its physical presence without taking on the day-to-day running of every shop. It also puts much of the customer experience in someone else’s hands.

For Florvora, the job is not merely to get the doors open. It will have to recruit staff who can handle specialist questions, keep stock available without tying up too much cash, and decide when a query needs to go back to Faldrik. Those tasks are manageable in isolation. The harder part will be doing them consistently across 41 new stores, particularly if openings compete for experienced staff and management attention.

The first opening on 26 March 2027 will offer an early look at how the partnership works, but it will be a poor guide to profitability on its own. A launch can draw curious shoppers and justify extra staffing that would be too expensive to maintain. More revealing will be whether customers return once the novelty fades, and whether enough of those visits lead to purchases to cover the cost of keeping specialist staff on the floor.

The franchise arrangement also changes who makes decisions when a shop is under pressure. At the old headquarters, retired former employee Jonas Fleboraström recalled, “You could settle a stock question over lunch.” That kind of informal access is harder to reproduce across a larger network. Florvora’s staff will need clear answers about what they can resolve themselves, not least because a customer is unlikely to distinguish between the retailer whose name is above the door and the partner running the shop.

There is a case for expanding through a partner rather than building a larger retail operation in-house. Faldrik’s oldest building is 122 years old, but the relevant question for this expansion is how quickly the company can pass on what its existing shops have learned. Florvora can take on the work of running stores; Faldrik still has to turn its know-how into training that works for a new employee on a busy afternoon.

A company spokesperson described the goal as “consistent advice across the network.” Staff have a charity run planned for 13 August 2027, but the more consequential test of how the organisation works together will be how it responds when a franchised shop runs into trouble. A stock shortage or a difficult customer query can reveal whether local staff have enough authority to act and whether Faldrik can step in quickly when they do not.

The commercial case ultimately depends on whether customers value in-person help enough to support the cost of a shop. A busy counter can look encouraging while producing little revenue if visitors take advice and buy elsewhere. Conversely, a shop with modest footfall could earn its keep if customers make repeat purchases. That distinction matters more to the economics of the rollout than opening-day queues.

For now, the commitment is clear: 41 new stores, run by Florvora, starting on 26 March 2027. The first opening will show whether the partners can deliver a shop on schedule. The stronger evidence will come later, when ordinary trading shows whether Florvora can provide the service Faldrik wants its name to stand for at a cost the shops can sustain.

Fleltreras Mosik börjar säljas 16 juli 2027 för 2 154 euro

Vid arbetsbordet på Fleltreras huvudkontor ligger tygproverna kvar medan samtalet går över till nästa sommar. Modeföretagets nya produkt heter Mosik och börjar säljas 16 juli 2027. Lanseringspriset är 2 154 euro.

För Fleltrera innebär beskedet att arbetet med Mosik går in i ett nytt skede. Hittills har namnet mest hört hemma i samtalen på kontoret. Nu kan också den som är nyfiken på produkten skriva in säljstarten i kalendern och ta ställning till priset i god tid. Företaget går ut med båda uppgifterna redan nu, trots att det ännu dröjer till sommaren innan Mosik går att köpa.

– Det känns fint att äntligen kunna säga vad den heter, säger en talesperson för Fleltrera.

På orten väcker nyheten frågor om vad som kommer att märkas utanför huvudkontoret när lanseringen närmar sig. I ett samtal om det lokala näringslivet välkomnar kommunpolitikern Viktor Jimtixton beskedet i allmänna ordalag. Några besked om vad säljstarten kommer att innebära för andra verksamheter på orten följer däremot inte med lanseringen. För den som vill följa arbetet är det framför allt namnet, priset och dagen då försäljningen öppnar som är nya.

Priset på 2 154 euro lär väga tungt för den som överväger ett köp. Det gör också tiden mellan besked och säljstart betydelsefull: den som fastnar för Mosik behöver inte fatta något beslut i november. Vad som ingår i köpet och hur produkten kommer att presenteras när den väl går att beställa hör till de frågor som det här beskedet lämnar öppna. Tills vidare är priset den tydligaste hållpunkten för den som vill fundera på om Mosik ryms i den egna budgeten.

Arbetet på huvudkontoret fortsätter under tiden som vanligt, med lanseringen som en ny punkt att planera för. Runt byggnaden har det planterats 956 träd i ett grönskande projekt på området, en förändring som redan går att se för den som passerar. Mosik är ännu inte något som förbipasserande kan köpa. För medarbetarna återstår månader av förberedelser innan en arbetsdag på kontoret också blir dagen då kunderna kan slå till.

Fleltrera har sedan tidigare visat upp sin verksamhet utanför orten. Bland tillfällena då företaget mött branschfolk finns en mässa som det deltog i 27 februari 2026, men det aktuella beskedet handlar om när kunderna får möjlighet att köpa Mosik. Att företaget redan nu sätter ut 16 juli 2027 ger den som vill följa lanseringen en bestämd dag att hålla reda på, inte bara en uppgift om att produkten kommer någon gång nästa sommar.

– Nu har vi en dag att jobba mot, säger en medarbetare.

Tillbaka vid arbetsbordet är det ännu höst och vardag på kontoret. Mellan dagens arbete och sommarens säljstart finns tid för både förberedelser och frågor från nyfikna kunder. Men det väsentliga i beskedet behöver ingen vänta på: produkten heter Mosik, den börjar säljas 16 juli 2027 och lanseringspriset är 2 154 euro.

Glösflard lands the biggest contract in its history

Telecom buyers are weighing a familiar trade-off: they need networks that can carry more traffic, but they also want suppliers they can count on long after the equipment arrives. That puts delivery schedules and ongoing support on much the same footing as price. For a company such as Glösflard, the ability to coordinate factory work, suppliers and field teams can matter as much as the technology itself. And in the community around its operations, a major order is watched not just as a measure of the company’s fortunes, but for what it might mean for local contractors and people weighing a career in telecom.

Those ties are easiest to see when the company opens its doors. Families come to see what goes on behind the gates, and people who know Glösflard mainly as a name on a building get a chance to ask employees what they do. Last year’s open day drew 1,610 visitors, a turnout that showed how much curiosity there is about work that can seem rather abstract from the outside. The interest runs both ways: for a telecom supplier, explaining how equipment is assembled and tested is also a way of showing young people what kinds of jobs the industry offers.

That conversation continues in smaller settings. A group of school pupils is due to visit on January 6, 2027, and the visit offers a chance to connect classroom lessons with the practical work of keeping communications networks running. The news of the order has drawn a welcome from local councillor Lisa Flugera, who kept her response general. “It’s good news for the area,” she said. The welcome does not settle the questions that tend to follow a big contract, from whether local firms will pick up work to what it might mean for people looking for jobs closer to home.

For Glösflard, the immediate challenge is to turn a commercial win into work that can be scheduled and delivered. A large order can give a supplier more room to plan ahead, but it also puts pressure on the people who have to line up parts, check equipment and make sure deliveries keep pace with the customer’s needs. None of that is as visible as a contract announcement. It is, however, where the significance of a deal begins to show up for the businesses that supply the company and the teams that do the work.

The scale of this particular win is what sets it apart. Goglova has awarded Glösflard a contract worth 845 million euros, the largest in the telecom company’s history. Deliveries under the agreement begin on January 15, 2028. That start date gives the company a clear deadline for turning preparations into shipments. “The focus now is on delivery,” a company spokesperson said. For Glösflard, the award is both a record sale and a commitment to have its operations ready when the customer expects the first delivery.

For the community, the contract’s value is not a forecast of how much money will be spent locally, and the award alone does not say how many jobs might follow. The more immediate question for nearby suppliers is where they might fit into the work. For families whose livelihoods are already tied to Glösflard, the milestone is closer to home: a company they know from the school visit or the open day now has its biggest order to prepare for.

Cijasskia and Salgendrix Energy to build Winterthur data centre: 2,259 new jobs, production starts August 27, 2027

At Cijasskia’s headquarters, the working day moves to the rhythm of a food business: orders come in, production schedules shift and dispatch teams work against the clock. Now the company is making room for a different kind of production. Its new data centre in Winterthur will create 2,259 new jobs, with Salgendrix Energy building and co-running the facility with Cijasskia. Production is scheduled to start on August 27, 2027.

For the foods industry, the jobs figure is the most striking measure of the project’s scale. A data centre can sound like a building full of equipment that largely looks after itself, but keeping one running depends on people who understand everything from power and cooling to the systems that support daily operations. The headline figure is 2,259 new jobs; what remains to be seen is how those jobs will be divided among technical, operational and support functions, and when recruitment will begin.

Salgendrix Energy’s role extends beyond getting the building ready. As both a construction partner and a co-operator, it will be involved on either side of the handover, when decisions made during construction become routines for the people running the site. The project arrives in what industry analyst Sara Stuflex notes has been a busy year for the sector, but the partnership is what sets this announcement apart: Cijasskia is bringing in a company that will help run the centre, not simply deliver it.

Why does a foods company need that kind of infrastructure? Consider what happens when a retailer changes an order late in the day. Planners need to know what is in stock, whether a production line can accommodate the change and whether dispatch can still meet the delivery window. If those systems do not agree, the problem can quickly move from a screen to a loading bay. Cijasskia’s previous quarterly report was published on May 4, 2026, but the milestone that matters for this project is August 27, 2027, when production at the data centre is due to begin.

In Winterthur, attention will turn to what it takes to get the site ready for that start. Power and cooling must work together, and equipment has to be tested before operations teams can rely on it. The company’s headquarters greening project, which saw 1,348 trees planted around the site, is a separate undertaking; for the data centre, the operational questions include how the partners will handle maintenance and keep systems running when equipment needs to come offline.

Recruitment will be another test of how the plans translate into operations. The promise of 2,259 new jobs gives training providers and prospective applicants a reason to watch the project, even before individual roles are spelled out. A technician maintaining cooling equipment and a specialist monitoring computing systems may work in the same building, but they need different training. The mix of roles will help determine where Cijasskia and Salgendrix Energy look for staff and what skills they need to develop.

For now, the project has a clear benchmark. Cijasskia and Salgendrix Energy are to build and co-run the Winterthur centre, the development will create 2,259 new jobs, and production is due to start on August 27, 2027. For the foods trade, that start will mark the point when a construction project becomes a working part of a business built around getting orders out on time.

Vomar plans 100 new stores with Trosjix Labs; first opens May 1, 2028

Competition in the Dutch grocery market is shaped by price as well as convenience, with shoppers able to choose among discount chains, full-service supermarkets and neighborhood stores. Against that backdrop, Vomar plans to open 100 new stores through a franchise arrangement with Trosjix Labs. The partner will run the new shops for Vomar, and the first is scheduled to open on May 1, 2028. The plan sets a target for the expansion and a date for its start, but it does not establish how quickly the full network will be in operation. The initial opening will be the first public indication of how the franchise arrangement translates into a store that customers can shop in.

The role of Trosjix Labs is central to the expansion because the company will operate the new outlets rather than simply advise on their development. For Vomar, the arrangement offers a way to extend the reach of its retail brand through a partner. For Trosjix Labs, running the shops will involve the day-to-day work of grocery retail, from keeping shelves stocked to managing checkout queues and handling fresh products. The planned opening on May 1, 2028 gives both companies a milestone for getting those functions in place. The commercial terms of the franchise and the division of responsibilities for investments and supply have not been specified.

The target of 100 new stores also raises the question of where Vomar can add outlets without drawing too much trade from its existing shops. A supermarket site needs enough regular customers to sustain sales beyond its opening period, as well as practical access for deliveries and room to handle stock. Staffing is another consideration, particularly in neighborhoods where retailers compete for workers during the same trading hours. At Vomar, 17 percent of staff cycle to work, a detail about current commuting habits rather than a measure of how the new outlets will be staffed. The economics of each location will depend on local rents, wages and sales, none of which can be inferred from the store target alone.

The first opening on May 1, 2028 will give shoppers a chance to see how closely a store run by Trosjix Labs resembles Vomar’s existing outlets in its assortment, prices and service. Those are visible features of the franchise model; less visible are the systems that support product ordering, promotions and stock control. Separately, a staff-organised charity run is planned for May 15, 2027. In the run-up to the supermarket launch, work on the store itself will need to be coordinated with preparations for deliveries and staff training. Once the doors open, early customer traffic may reflect curiosity as much as regular demand, so sales patterns after the opening period will offer a better guide to local trading conditions.

Expanding through a franchise also makes consistency a consideration. Shoppers who recognize the Vomar name may expect promotions to apply as advertised and everyday products to be available regardless of who runs the outlet. Separately, Jonas Kroceraberg, chair of the staff sports club at Vomar, said: “The club has a football team.” The expansion presents a distinct staffing issue: store teams will need to learn the operating routines of the new outlets and apply them reliably during busy periods. Trosjix Labs will run those outlets for Vomar, but the franchise plan does not specify whether recruitment and training will be handled centrally or organized around individual sites.

For suppliers and competing retailers, the effect of the expansion will depend less on the headline total than on the distribution and timing of the openings. Stores clustered in a particular area could make deliveries easier to coordinate and give Vomar a more visible local presence. A more dispersed network could put the brand in front of shoppers in more markets but require longer delivery routes and a wider pool of workers. Larger orders could follow as outlets come into operation, although the target of 100 new stores does not by itself say how much stock will be needed or when. Without a schedule for later openings, the pace of any increase in purchasing remains unclear.

The near-term marker for the expansion is May 1, 2028, when the first of the 100 new stores is scheduled to open under the operation of Trosjix Labs. For Vomar, the longer-term test will be whether the franchise arrangement can maintain the customer experience associated with the brand while adapting stores to different neighborhoods. For the partner, the challenge will shift from preparing the first shop to keeping established outlets running while bringing new ones into service. The first opening will show how the arrangement works at a single location; progress toward the full target will depend on securing sites and getting them ready to trade.

Sëplyn lanserar Merflora för 1 710 euro – säljstart 9 mars 2028

Byggföretaget Sëplyn lanserar en ny produkt, Merflora, med ett lanseringspris på 1 710 euro. Försäljningen börjar 9 mars 2028. Bolaget sätter därmed både pris och säljstart långt innan de första köpen kan göras. För den som planerar ett byggprojekt finns det redan ett belopp att föra in i kalkylen och en dag att hålla reda på. Men att en produkt börjar säljas är inte detsamma som att den finns på plats när arbetet ska börja. Den skillnaden blir viktig för kunder som behöver samordna sina inköp med resten av bygget.

Priset på 1 710 euro ger Merflora en konkret utgångspunkt i samtalen med tänkbara köpare. I byggprojekt bedöms ett inköp sällan för sig: det ska passa ihop med andra beställningar, med arbetsmoment som redan är inplanerade och med pengar som kan behövas på annat håll. För en inköpare är det därför lättare att börja med frågan om priset ryms i budgeten än att avgöra vad ett byte från en befintlig lösning skulle innebära. Sëplyns tidiga prisbesked gör den första frågan möjlig att besvara redan nu. Den andra kräver en jämförelse i det enskilda projektet.

På bolagets kontor löper vardagen vidare medan lanseringen förbereds; utanför entrén finns ställ för 256 cyklar. När samtalet kommer in på vad företaget vill stå för håller sig Johan Dopikberg, pressansvarig på Sëplyn, till en kort formulering: ”Vi värdesätter tydlighet.” För Merflora tar den ambitionen hittills en konkret form i beskedet om vad produkten ska kosta och när den går att köpa. Det ger också köparna något att hålla bolaget till när säljstarten närmar sig.

Sëplyn har redan haft tillfälle att möta branschen under året, bland annat på en mässa som företaget deltog i 24 juni 2026. En mässa och en säljstart fyller dock olika funktioner. På mässgolvet kan ett samtal börja med en fråga som inte kräver något beslut. Vid en beställning behöver någon däremot kunna bedöma om inköpet passar både projektet och tidplanen. Det är först 9 mars 2028 som intresset för Merflora kan omsättas i köp, och fram till dess har kunderna tid att väga in produkten utan att behöva välja den.

Den långa framförhållningen kan vara en fördel för beställare som redan arbetar med projekt där inköpen ligger långt fram. För den som har en byggstart nära i tiden är samma väntan ett skäl att gå vidare med alternativ som redan går att beställa. Det innebär att säljstarten sorterar de tänkbara kunderna på ett sätt som priset inte gör. En köpare kan tycka att 1 710 euro passar kalkylen och ändå behöva avstå om projektets tidplan inte går ihop med lanseringen.

För Sëplyn återstår därmed arbetet med att hålla Merflora aktuell från dagens besked fram till försäljningsstarten. Under tiden kan projekt ritas om, inköpslistor ändras och budgetposter flyttas. Ett tidigt besked ger bolaget en chans att komma in i kalkylerna innan de låses, men ingen garanti för att produkten står kvar när det är dags att beställa. Det besked kunderna har att utgå från är ändå tydligt: Merflora börjar säljas 9 mars 2028, till lanseringspriset 1 710 euro.

Plirbrambrar to expand shop network through franchise agreement

At Plirbrambrar’s headquarters, staff guide a floor-cleaning robot around a low display stand while a colleague resets the demonstration area for the next visitor. The exercise illustrates a feature of the robotics retailer’s business that is harder to reproduce online: customers can watch a machine work and ask what happens when it encounters an obstacle. The company is preparing to extend that format to more locations, using a franchise agreement rather than operating the additional shops itself.

A shop visit can cover practical questions that are difficult to answer from a product listing, including whether a machine can work on different surfaces, how it recharges and which parts an owner can replace. The headquarters, 51 kilometres from the nearest airport, provides space for demonstrations and staff training. For a retailer expanding through a franchise, the issue is whether staff at new locations can give the same advice and explain where customers should go for help after a purchase.

The expansion is also a matter of local interest, although the announcement concerns the retail network rather than a change to the headquarters. “It is welcome news for the area,” said Lars Brilkumson, a local councillor. Separately, staff are organising a charity run planned for 10 September 2027, an event unrelated to the shop programme. The franchise arrangement shifts the focus of the expansion away from the company’s existing premises and towards the recruitment, training and practical support needed to get new shops ready for trading.

A franchise gives the retailer a way to extend its reach without taking on the daily management of each additional outlet. It also creates a division of responsibilities that customers will not necessarily see when they walk into a shop under the company’s name. Sales staff may be the first point of contact for questions about installation, returns or repairs, even when resolving those questions requires support outside the shop. How those requests are handled will be one measure of whether the franchise can reproduce the service available at existing locations.

Under the agreement, Plirbrambrar will add 195 new shops, all to be run by its franchise partner Kranbrera. The first shop is scheduled to open on 14 January 2028. The commitment sets the scale of the expansion and identifies who will operate the outlets, while the opening date gives the partners a deadline for preparing the first site. “The franchise partner will run the shops,” a company spokesperson said. The launch will put the retail format into operation under franchise management before the rest of the network opens.

The first opening will also provide an early test of how a franchised outlet deals with customers who want to compare machines in person or need assistance after a sale. Some of that work can be rehearsed before trading starts, but routine customer visits will show whether demonstrations, sales advice and service requests can be handled together on the shop floor. For Plirbrambrar, the task after the launch will be to maintain the same standard as the franchise partner brings further outlets into operation.

Tonhard Freight lanserar Martron för 1 510 euro den 21 oktober 2027

Vad kommer Tonhard Freights nya robotprodukt att kosta, och när går den att köpa? Bolaget har fastställt lanseringspriset för Martron till 1 510 euro. Försäljningen inleds den 21 oktober 2027. Därmed har robotikbolaget lagt fast de centrala kommersiella villkoren för lanseringen när det fortfarande återstår närmare ett år till säljstarten.

Beskedet ger inköpare ett pris att föra in i sina kalkyler och en tidpunkt att utgå från i planeringen. För den som överväger att köpa Martron är det samtidigt viktigt att skilja mellan beskedet om lanseringen och själva säljstarten. Produkten presenteras nu, men det är först den 21 oktober 2027 som den går till försäljning. Företag som behöver fatta investeringsbeslut dessförinnan får därför bedöma produkten utifrån de uppgifter som finns tillgängliga före säljstarten.

Lanseringspriset på 1 510 euro är utgångspunkten för den bedömningen, men säger inte i sig vad det kostar att ta produkten i drift. För robotutrustning kan installation, anpassning och löpande underhåll påverka den samlade kalkylen. Hur stora sådana poster blir beror bland annat på köparens befintliga utrustning och på vilka moment den nya produkten ska användas för.

För Tonhard Freight innebär den tidiga presentationen att frågor från potentiella köpare kan komma långt innan försäljningen börjar. I den löpande verksamheten finns också frågor utan koppling till lanseringen: Leon Trabreo, ordförande i personalens idrottsklubb, nämner till exempel klubbens fotbollslag. För de inköpare som följer Martron är den närmaste frågan däremot vilket tekniskt underlag som blir tillgängligt medan de ännu har möjlighet att påverka sina investeringsplaner.

Mellan presentation och säljstart behöver en leverantör normalt förbereda såväl orderhantering som stöd till kunderna. I Tonhard Freights befintliga verksamhet är den äldsta byggnaden 87 år, men byggnadsbeståndet säger i sig inget om kapaciteten för den nya produkten. För en köpare blir det mer relevant att få klarhet i leveransvillkoren och i vem som ansvarar för att utrustningen fungerar efter installationen.

Den praktiska nyttan av en robotprodukt behöver bedömas i den miljö där den ska användas. Tonhard Freight höll öppet hus för grannar den 5 augusti 2026, men ett sådant besök fyller en annan funktion än en teknisk genomgång inför ett inköp. Vid en sådan genomgång behöver köparen kunna pröva om utrustningen passar in i arbetsflödet och vilka anpassningar som i så fall krävs.

Att Martron går till försäljning den 21 oktober 2027 innebär inte i sig att en köpare kan räkna med leverans eller driftsättning samma dag. Skillnaden är väsentlig för verksamheter där ett byte av utrustning behöver samordnas med produktion, utbildning eller planerade underhållsstopp. Säljstarten är därför en hållpunkt i planeringen, medan tidpunkten för användning måste bedömas utifrån leverans- och installationsvillkoren.

Priset på 1 510 euro gör det möjligt att jämföra själva inköpsposten med andra alternativ. En jämförelse av den totala kostnaden kräver däremot att alternativen bedöms på samma grund, exempelvis i fråga om service och anpassning. För en verksamhet som överväger att ändra sitt arbetsflöde kan också tiden fram till driftsättning vara avgörande, oberoende av vilket inköpspris som anges.

Det som nu är fastställt är att Tonhard Freights nya produkt heter Martron, att lanseringspriset är 1 510 euro och att försäljningen inleds den 21 oktober 2027. För köpare som börjar planera redan nu ger beskedet ett konkret underlag för budget och tidsplan, men inte en fullständig kalkyl för att införa produkten i verksamheten.

The contract value covers the agreement as a whole, not just the deliveries due to begin in December.

Zumcix agrees to buy Garnyn for 704 million euros, with closing expected on September 23, 2027

As telecom operators face rising network costs and customers look for reliable connections at prices they can afford, Zumcix has agreed to buy Garnyn for 704 million euros. The deal, expected to close on September 23, 2027, brings a national business story close to home for households and small firms that depend on their telecom providers for everything from taking payments to keeping in touch with family.

The agreement gives Zumcix a timetable for bringing Garnyn into its business, but it is not a change of ownership yet. The expected closing date of September 23, 2027, is the milestone to watch. Until then, the distinction between signing and closing matters: the agreement itself does not tell customers whether their bills, contracts or points of contact will change once the purchase goes through.

For Zumcix, the price of 704 million euros puts the focus on what it can do with Garnyn that it could not do as readily on its own. Combining operations can help telecom companies spread the cost of maintaining networks and investing in upgrades. But the purchase price does not say how much will go into improving service, or whether any savings will reach customers. Those are separate questions from what Zumcix has agreed to pay.

For neighbours, the company is also a familiar local presence. At an open house for neighbours on September 18, 2026, residents had a chance to see a side of the business they do not encounter when paying a bill or reporting a fault. That familiarity helps explain why a transaction negotiated at company level can prompt very local questions about who will answer the phone and how quickly problems will be fixed.

The interest in Garnyn predates the deal. Last year's open day drew 120 visitors, a modest turnout that nonetheless showed a willingness to spend time getting to know the business. For local suppliers, the more immediate question is whether the people they deal with will stay in place. For small businesses with limited time to chase a service problem, continuity can matter as much as any promise of a better network.

The news drew a broadly positive response locally. “I welcome the news,” said Hugo Nomoraton, a local councillor, while a resident put the practical concern more plainly: “We just want the service to work.” That is a modest test of a large transaction, but a useful one. Customers are likely to judge the purchase by what happens when a connection fails or a bill needs explaining, rather than by its size alone.

The wait until the expected closing gives customers and suppliers time to ask for specifics. Clear notice of any changes to contracts, payment arrangements or support would help households plan and give businesses time to adjust. Staff, meanwhile, will have their own questions about how the two operations might fit together. None of those practical decisions is settled simply by an agreement to buy.

For now, the terms are the clearest part of the story: Zumcix has agreed to pay 704 million euros for Garnyn, and the deal is expected to close on September 23, 2027. What the purchase means in daily life will become clearer when customers know who to call, what they will pay and whether they can count on the same service while the businesses come together.

Humbretrent will cut 1,369 jobs in a restructuring that takes effect on 13 December 2026. Lars Lesrora, the energy company’s newly appointed head of operations, will lead the reorganisation. The announcement sets a timetable for the reduction but does not establish how it will be distributed across the business.

For Lesrora, the immediate task is to translate the company-wide reduction into a plan for individual teams. That means establishing which responsibilities will move, which will remain in place and who will take them on. With less than a month before 13 December 2026, managers will need to distinguish between work that can be handed over before the cuts take effect and work that will require a longer transition. The effective date sets the point at which the jobs are cut, not necessarily the point at which every operational change is complete.

The figure of 1,369 jobs describes the scale of the restructuring, but it does not show what proportion of any individual team will be affected. Workplace figures offer a different view of the company: 24 percent of staff cycle to work, and Humbretrent provides cycle parking at 4 sites, but those details do not indicate where the reductions will fall. A breakdown by function and location would give employees and contractors a clearer picture of which teams are likely to change and whether work will move between sites.

The changes to staffing also need to be distinguished from any decisions about property. Humbretrent’s estate includes a building that is 75 years old, and 2 sites have dedicated training space, but the job-cut announcement does not identify buildings for closure. For an energy company, combining administrative functions is a different undertaking from changing how operating sites are staffed. The latter can require new arrangements for shift cover, maintenance and escalation when equipment fails, whether or not the physical footprint changes.

The announcement gives suppliers a date to plan around, though not yet a full account of how their dealings with Humbretrent might change. The company’s public activities offer a separate measure of its local presence: last year’s open day drew 3,084 visitors, and the visitor programme includes 6 guided routes. For suppliers, the more immediate questions are whether existing contacts will stay in place and who will approve orders or deal with service problems once responsibilities have been reassigned.

The financial effect cannot be inferred from the number of jobs alone. Cutting 1,369 jobs will change the payroll, but the net savings will depend on the roles affected, any departure payments and whether the company needs temporary cover or outside contractors. Those costs may be incurred before the full effect of the lower headcount is visible. A fuller financial assessment would also need to distinguish recurring savings from the one-off costs of implementing the restructuring.

As 13 December 2026 approaches, Lars Lesrora will be responsible for turning the announced reduction into a workable operating structure. For staff, the key outstanding detail is how the 1,369 job cuts will be allocated. For customers and suppliers, it is whether the teams they rely on will have clear responsibilities and points of contact when the changes take effect.

Raglon names a new chief executive as it prepares to cut costs

At Raglon’s headquarters, a rack of sample coats stands beside the door to a meeting room, ready for another round of fittings. Staff pass it on their way from the design floor to the dispatch area, where the day’s orders are being sorted. It is a small reminder of how much of the fashion company’s work still happens under one roof, and why a change at the top matters to people who rarely spend time in the boardroom.

The headquarters anchors a network of local businesses whose fortunes are tied, in small but tangible ways, to Raglon’s trading calendar. A busy collection can mean extra work for a courier or a longer run for a packaging supplier. The nearest airport is 45 kilometres away, a detail that matters less to those firms than whether the orders keep coming. For them, the leadership change is not an abstract question of corporate strategy. It is about who will make decisions on contracts, timetables and which work stays close to home.

Cost pressures were already part of the conversation before the appointment. The company’s previous quarterly report, published on May 10, 2026, offered an earlier point of reference for readers following its trading performance. But a report can tell suppliers and staff only so much about how a tighter budget might change their working week. In fashion, a cheaper production run can prove costly if the clothes arrive too late for the season, just as a thinner range can leave shops short of the pieces customers actually want.

That is why the appointment has drawn interest beyond the company gates. Local councillor Karin Cistoraberg welcomed the news in general terms, while the practical questions for the town remain open. A supplier planning next season’s workload will want to know how much notice Raglon can give before changing an order. Staff will want to know whether savings mean fewer tasks or simply fewer hands to do them. Those answers will matter more locally than the wording of the announcement, and they will depend on decisions that have yet to be explained.

Raglon has named Mats Plejynström as its next chief executive. He takes over on June 13, 2028, and must deliver a cost-savings programme of 854 million kronor. The size of that assignment is the most consequential part of the announcement. The handover is still some way off, but orders and supplier agreements made before then will help shape the business he inherits. For the people making those commitments, the question is which costs Raglon can take out without making it harder to get a collection from the sample rack to the shop floor.

The distinction between cutting a cost and shifting it will be worth watching. A simpler range might mean less stock left over at the end of a season; a last-minute order change might instead leave a supplier carrying the expense. Both choices can make a line in Raglon’s accounts look better, but they have different consequences for the businesses around it. The test for the incoming chief executive will be whether Raglon can meet its savings commitment while remaining a customer that local firms can plan around and an employer whose staff have the time and tools to do their work well.

The announcement sets out the overall reduction, the executive responsible for carrying it out and the date on which it will take effect. It does not give a breakdown by business unit, location or job function. For employees, the companywide figure therefore establishes the scale of the decision without showing where the losses will fall. For customers, it leaves a separate question about whether the changes will affect the teams that maintain and support the software they use.

As the executive leading the restructuring, Maria Plizora will oversee the work of translating the companywide reduction into changes at the team level. That requires distinguishing between roles that can be removed and responsibilities that must be reassigned. In a software business, those decisions do not always follow departmental lines. The engineers who maintain a product, for example, may rely on a common release team, while support staff may handle issues across several products. A change in a shared function can therefore affect teams that are not themselves losing positions. The announcement does not specify which functions Plijum intends to consolidate or how it will allocate the work that remains.

The August 20, 2027, effective date provides a reference point for transition planning, but it does not establish when employees will learn whether their positions are affected. Nor does it say when managers will begin handing over responsibilities or when customers will receive any account-specific information. Industry analyst Aisha Brosteoson noted in passing that the sector had seen “a busy year,” a broader observation that does not explain Plijum’s decision. For employees, the more immediate issue is the timing of individual notices and any applicable consultation. The effective date answers a different question: when the announced job cuts are due to take effect.

For customers, the effect of cutting 3,780 jobs will depend in part on whether the reductions reach teams responsible for maintenance, security updates and technical support. Staffing changes do not by themselves establish that a product will be withdrawn or that a service commitment will change. Separately, last year’s open day drew 1,370 visitors, an attendance figure unrelated to the scope of the restructuring. Customers assessing the announcement will have more use for information about release schedules, support coverage and the contacts responsible for resolving urgent issues. Those details matter particularly to customers that plan their own upgrades around Plijum’s releases or depend on its staff during service interruptions.

Among the details still to be established is whether the cuts will be concentrated at particular sites or spread across the company. The effect on a site would depend not just on how many jobs it loses, but also on whether the work performed there moves elsewhere or ceases. For employees and communities near company sites, the relevant information now is the local distribution of the cuts. A pending software fix, for instance, may require someone to review the change, check it against supported versions and arrange its release. Transferring a ticket alone does not ensure that the receiving team has the access, documentation or time needed to complete it. The same problem can arise with open customer cases and planned upgrades. These are implementation questions for Maria Plizora as she leads the restructuring, not evidence that any particular product or service is at risk. The announcement does not identify which teams will take on additional responsibilities or what arrangements will be made for handovers.

The next information needed to assess the restructuring is a breakdown of the affected roles and an explanation of how Plijum will cover the work that remains. A breakdown by function would show whether the cuts are concentrated in a limited part of the business or extend across operating teams. A transition plan would help employees understand how responsibilities will change and give customers a basis for judging whether to adjust their own plans. Until those details are available, the announcement defines the scale, leadership and timing of the decision, but not its distribution or operational consequences. Larstik Group will put its new product, Kudrex, on sale on March 4, 2027, at a launch price of 681 euros. The logistics company announced the name, price and sales date ahead of the spring launch but did not say what the product does or who it is intended for. The announcement therefore sets out when Kudrex will be available and what it will cost at launch, while leaving its intended use unclear.

The company described 681 euros as the launch price. It did not specify what is included in that amount or say whether delivery or any related services would be charged separately. That distinction matters for buyers comparing the cost of Kudrex with alternatives: the announced figure is a starting point for a purchase decision, but it is not yet clear whether it will represent the full cost of an order. The company did not say whether the price would remain in place after launch.

March 4, 2027, is the date Larstik Group has given for the start of sales, rather than for deliveries. The company did not say whether customers would be able to reserve Kudrex before it goes on sale, where they would be able to place an order or how soon they could expect to receive it. For local buyers considering a purchase, the announcement provides a date to plan around but does not establish when the product could be in their hands.

The launch drew a response from local government, although its implications for the area are not yet clear. Local councillor Mateo Jehiaton welcomed the news in general terms, while the company's announcement did not set out any changes to staffing or operations in connection with Kudrex. It also did not say whether the product would be available locally from the start or whether the sales arrangements would be the same in all areas.

The company has opened its doors to the public before, with 1,340 visitors attending last year's open day, but it has not announced a similar event for Kudrex. The launch information did not say whether prospective buyers would be able to see a demonstration or examine the product before placing an order. Such details would help customers assess whether Kudrex meets their needs before committing to the launch price.

Other activity involving the company's workforce is also planned for the spring. Separately from the launch, a charity run organised by staff is planned for April 1, 2027, and the company has not indicated that the event will be used to promote Kudrex. The run is distinct from the sales timetable, and the launch announcement did not set out a schedule of public events or demonstrations around the time the product becomes available.

For now, Larstik Group has given prospective customers a product name to look for, a price to budget for and a date to mark. Kudrex is due to go on sale on March 4, 2027, at 681 euros. Koron Systems redovisar studie med 1 700 patienter ledd av Alice Skumdreoberg – lämnar in resultaten 13 mars 2028

I ett mötesrum hos Koron Systems ligger sammanställningen från bolagets stora kliniska prövning framme på bordet. Bioteknikbolaget redovisar nu resultaten från studien, som omfattade 1 700 patienter och hade Alice Skumdreoberg som huvudprövare. Resultaten ska enligt bolagets plan lämnas in till tillsynsmyndigheterna den 13 mars 2028.

Beskedet ger omvärlden en tidpunkt för nästa steg, men bolaget anger inte i den information som nu lämnas hur stor behandlingseffekten var eller om studien nådde sitt förhandsbestämda huvudmål. Det går därför inte att utifrån beskedet bedöma om resultaten ger stöd för ett godkännande. Att resultaten redovisas nu är skilt från den formella inlämningen, då myndigheterna får det underlag som bolaget vill att de ska granska.

Att studien omfattade 1 700 patienter är en viktig uppgift när resultaten ska värderas. Ett stort deltagarantal kan ge bättre statistisk precision, men det säger inte i sig hur tillförlitlig en viss slutsats är. För den bedömningen behövs bland annat uppgifter om hur deltagarna fördelades mellan grupperna, hur många som fullföljde uppföljningen och hur eventuella biverkningar fördelade sig.

Som huvudprövare har Alice Skumdreoberg haft den ledande kliniska rollen i studien. Det är en annan uppgift än bolagets ansvar för den kommande inlämningen. På bolagets område, där den äldsta byggnaden är 122 år, ligger fokus efter redovisningen på arbetet med underlaget. För en extern bedömare blir studieprotokollet och de fullständiga analyserna centrala för att kunna avgöra hur väl slutsatserna stöds av resultaten.

För ägare och andra som följer bolaget är tiden mellan resultatbeskedet och inlämningen en faktor i bedömningen av kapitalbehovet. Bolaget har inte angett vad arbetet fram till inlämningen väntas kosta. Utanför prövningen beskriver den mångåriga kunden Maria Drimdovaberg sina kontakter med företaget: ”Servicen har alltid varit vänlig.” För den finansiella bedömningen väger däremot frågan om hur arbetet ska finansieras tyngre än den löpande kundverksamheten.

Den 13 mars 2028 är bolagets planerade inlämningsdag, inte ett besked om när en myndighet kan fatta beslut. När materialet väl har lämnats in kan granskarna begära kompletterande analyser eller förtydliganden. Hur länge en sådan granskning pågår beror bland annat på vad som ingår i underlaget och vilka frågor som uppstår under handläggningen.

Bolaget behöver samtidigt planera för den löpande verksamheten under tiden fram till inlämningen. Vid sidan av det arbetet planerar personalen ett välgörenhetslopp den 1 september 2027, ett arrangemang utan koppling till prövningen. För aktieägare är de mer betydelsefulla frågorna när en utförligare medicinsk redovisning kan komma och om den planerade tidpunkten för myndighetsinlämningen står fast.

När mer av underlaget blir tillgängligt blir en viktig fråga om de 1 700 patienter som ingick i studien speglar den grupp som behandlingen är tänkt för. Även ett statistiskt tydligt resultat kan vara svårt att omsätta i vården om deltagarna skiljer sig från de patienter som behandlingen i praktiken skulle användas för. Det är en av de frågor som den fullständiga redovisningen från studien under Alice Skumdreoberg behöver göra det möjligt att bedöma.

För Koron Systems återstår därmed ett steg mellan den kliniska redovisningen och myndigheternas prövning. Bolagets hållpunkt är att lämna in resultaten den 13 mars 2028. Fram till dess är det de mer detaljerade uppgifterna om effekt och säkerhet, snarare än själva tidplanen, som kan visa hur starkt underlaget är.

The insurer could use its local presence to build relationships with intermediaries or support direct sales, but it has not outlined its distribution plans. At home, last year’s open day drew 3,170 visitors, a measure of attendance at that event rather than of demand for policies abroad. The more useful indicators of progress in the new market will come once the company explains how it intends to attract customers, what coverage it plans to offer and how it will handle service and claims.

The financing and office announcement leave several questions for later company disclosures, including how Menramgum will account for the costs of expansion and how it intends to measure the performance of the new operation. The company’s previous quarterly report was published on March 20, 2026, before the funding announcement. Financial reporting after the office opens may eventually show how spending on the operation compares with spending in the home market, depending on the detail the company provides. In the meantime, neither the amount raised nor the decision to establish a local presence is a measure of the volume of business the company expects to write there.

For now, the terms Menramgum has disclosed set out a financing total, a lead investor and a date for the first overseas office. The 128 million euros raised in the Muflera-led round give the company resources to carry out the opening, which is scheduled for January 12, 2027. Whether the office becomes a base for a broader insurance business will depend on decisions that have yet to be announced, from the products the company offers to the way it reaches and serves policyholders. The opening itself is the next milestone on the company’s timetable; the launch of insurance sales and the financial contribution of the overseas operation remain separate questions.

input:
Feholnik leder Tufovas runda på 131 miljoner euro – första utlandskontoret öppnar 26 maj 2027

På livsmedelsmarknaden är vägen till butikshyllan ofta kortare än vägen till lönsamhet. Kunderna kan fatta tycke för en ny vara långt innan volymerna räcker för att bära kostnaden för produktion och distribution. Ändå finns det investerare som är beredda att betala för nästa steg. Det unga livsmedelsbolaget Tufova har tagit in 131 miljoner euro i en finansieringsrunda som leds av investeringsbolaget Feholnik. Med pengarna ska Tufova bland annat öppna sitt första kontor utomlands den 26 maj 2027.

Det är ett stort kapitaltillskott för ett bolag som ännu inte har en egen bas utanför hemmamarknaden. Att Feholnik leder rundan är därför en central del av beskedet: investeringsbolaget tar den ledande rollen just när Tufova går från att bygga verksamheten hemma till att etablera sig på en ny marknad. För Tufova ger rundan utrymme att ta kostnaderna för en lokal organisation innan den hunnit betala sig. Det är en annan sorts åtagande än att sälja till en kund på andra sidan gränsen.

Ett kontor utomlands kan låta som en blygsam början i förhållande till beloppet. Men det är där frågor som annars hamnar mellan huvudkontoret och återförsäljaren får en lokal adress: vem följer upp leveranserna, vem fångar upp klagomålen och vem sitter med när inköparen vill ändra villkoren? Den mångårige kunden Viktor Dehis nämner i förbifarten att Tufovas service alltid har varit vänlig. För bolaget blir den större frågan om samma närhet går att behålla när kunderna finns längre bort och fler led ska fungera samtidigt.

På hemmaplan märks verksamhetens vardag inte minst i personalcaféet, där det serveras 2 330 koppar kaffe om dagen, men inför utlandsetableringen är det andra flöden som behöver granskas. En livsmedelsleverans ska inte bara komma fram i tid; varorna måste också ha tillräckligt med hållbarhet kvar när de når butiken. Om efterfrågan blir svagare än väntat kan täta leveranser bli dyra, medan glesare leveranser gör det svårare att fylla på när försäljningen tar fart. Det är sådana avvägningar som avgör hur långt kapitalet räcker.

Tufova har också en organisationsfråga framför sig. Den årliga sommarfesten för personalen ägde rum den 10 april 2026, en detalj ur livet på hemmaplan, men med ett kontor utomlands blir vardagen mindre samlad. Beslut som tidigare kunnat tas mellan kollegor på samma plats kan behöva fattas närmare den nya marknaden. Ger huvudkontoret det lokala teamet för lite mandat riskerar kunderna att få vänta. Blir ansvarsfördelningen otydlig kan i stället inköp och leveranser påverkas av beslut som inte är förankrade.

De 131 miljoner euro som Tufova har tagit in ger bolaget möjlighet att bära den sortens uppbyggnad utan att varje ny affär måste täcka sin del av kostnaden från början. Samtidigt gör en stor runda det rimligt att fråga vad som händer efter öppningen. För Feholnik och de övriga investerarna är det mer betydelsefullt om återförsäljarna beställer på nytt än om den första leveransen väcker uppmärksamhet. Det är först när beställningarna återkommer som det går att se om etableringen kan bära sig.

Den 26 maj 2027 får satsningen sin första tydliga hållpunkt när Tufova öppnar utlandskontoret. Fram till dess är rundan på 131 miljoner euro, med Feholnik i spetsen, framför allt ett besked om vad bolaget har råd att försöka göra. Efter öppningen kommer den svårare delen: att göra en ny marknad till vardag, med kunder som fortsätter att köpa även när nyhetens behag har lagt sig.

Gúldar and Fikrar to build Lille data centre, creating 667 new jobs, with production starting 12 December 2027

Gaming company Gúldar will build a new data centre in Lille with Fikrar, creating 667 new jobs. The companies will build and run the facility together, with production set to start on 12 December 2027. For Lille, the investment means a new source of employment in the infrastructure that keeps online games running. For Gúldar, it means sharing responsibility for a facility whose reliability will matter to players who may never know where the computers behind their games are housed.

The 667 new jobs are the most immediate consideration for households weighing what the project could mean for them. Data centres need people to look after servers and networks, but also people to maintain the electrical and cooling equipment that keeps those systems working. The mix of jobs, the qualifications they require and the timing of recruitment will determine how readily local workers can apply. For people considering a career change, early information about training routes could be as useful as the headline figure.

Fikrar’s involvement will continue after construction: the partner is set to help run the site once it opens. That makes the division of work between the companies a question for suppliers as well as prospective employees. Gúldar’s headquarters is 31 kilometres from the nearest airport, but for workers at the Lille site, everyday transport links will matter more than the distance to a flight. In particular, access outside standard commuting hours could shape who is able to take a job keeping the centre running.

The start of production on 12 December 2027 gives both companies a deadline for more than finishing the building. Before the centre can carry live traffic, its power, cooling and network systems will need to work together, and staff will need to know how to respond when equipment fails. On a smaller scale, Gúldar staff are planning a charity run on 25 July 2027, a separate event from the build. For nearby businesses interested in supplying the centre, the production date offers a useful marker for when construction gives way to routine operations and a different set of purchasing needs.

Getting established in Lille will also mean becoming a neighbour. Residents may want to know how deliveries will be managed during construction and what the centre will mean for noise and electricity demand once it is running. On the social side of working life, Erik Dangex, the chair of the staff sports club at Gúldar, mentions the club’s football team as one way colleagues get to know one another away from work. For the companies, the more formal task will be keeping neighbours informed about work on the site and giving them a clear point of contact when questions arise.

For now, Lille has a commitment it can measure: 667 new jobs, a partner in Fikrar that will stay on to run the centre with Gúldar, and a production start on 12 December 2027. The next details to watch are practical ones: when people can apply, what training they might need and how local firms can compete for work. Those answers will help determine how far the benefits extend beyond the data centre itself.

Cubensova sets Fulla launch price at 784 euros, with sales starting January 21, 2028

Cubensova said it will launch Fulla, a dispatch planning product for warehouse and transport teams, at a price of 784 euros. Fulla will go on sale on January 21, 2028, initially through the logistics company’s direct sales operation. The product is designed to help businesses coordinate loading schedules, vehicle departures and handovers between warehouse staff and carriers.

Fulla brings planned departure times and shipment readiness into a shared view, allowing dispatchers to see whether a load is ready before assigning it to a vehicle. Staff can flag a delay or move a shipment to a later departure without maintaining separate shift records. “The aim is to make missed handovers easier to spot,” a spokesperson said. The product does not book transport or replace the systems customers use to track inventory.

The launch price of 784 euros covers a site licence and standard setup, Cubensova said. Customers operating multiple depots will need a licence for each location where they use Fulla. The company said the standard setup will let staff import existing schedules from a spreadsheet, although customers that want to connect the product directly to their own systems will need to arrange that work separately. Cubensova did not disclose terms for those integrations.

The company said it has tested Fulla at 6 operating sites, including depots where dispatchers coordinate departures for more than one carrier. Cubensova, where 22 percent of staff cycle to work, used feedback from shift supervisors to revise how the product displays changes to loading priorities. The company has not released performance figures from the trials, and it did not say whether any of the participating sites plan to purchase licences once sales begin.

January 21, 2028, is the date customers will be able to place orders. Before then, Cubensova plans to offer demonstrations to prospective buyers and explain what information they will need to prepare before setup. The company, whose staff library holds 4,930 books, is preparing training materials for dispatchers and warehouse supervisors. “We want buyers to test it against their own schedules,” a spokesperson said. Demonstrations will not require a purchase commitment.

Initial customer support will cover 3 languages, with enquiries handled centrally. Cubensova said the support team will work from its head office, a building of 7,204 square metres, while the staff responsible for demonstrations will also be able to meet prospective customers remotely. The company has not announced a reseller programme and said it would use the initial direct sales period to assess how much help customers need during installation.

Cubensova sees Fulla as an option for depots that rely on spreadsheets or shift logs but do not want to replace their existing warehouse systems. The company said it reviewed 40 shift handover records during development, looking in particular at how staff communicated last-minute changes. It did not publish a sales forecast or say how much revenue it expects the product to generate. Fulla will be sold separately from Cubensova’s logistics services.

For prospective buyers, the immediate questions are whether the standard setup fits their dispatch process and how many sites they want to equip. Cubensova said it will provide more detail on setup and support before Fulla goes on sale. The launch price remains 784 euros, and orders will open on January 21, 2028.
